policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'all their iniquity' permits both the qere לְכָל and ketiv לכול; no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them, so the documented qere base fallback is retained.

ASV 'I will cause their captivity to return' explicitly uses causative wording, distinguishing qere אָשִׁיב from ketiv אשוב. The note 'return to their captivity' is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the textual reading.
